hypothesis: A small additional supervised replay of the two regressed anchor windows can improve anchor reconstruction without substantially worsening the high-change h9 group, compared with the same checkpoint, main examples, optimizer state and update count without replay.
main_pair_selection: (start + horizon) % 2 == 0; 4 or 5 horizons per start and exactly 84 windows per horizon
anchor_replay_loss: Same RGB + 0.1 * state loss as the main objective, with its own real future supervision and the same initial-only decoder condition
evaluation: 18 anchor future predictions and all 168 h9 predictions per arm, eight fixed panels, no independent native GS replay
exploratory_gate: Anchor 18-frame motion MAE <= 0.90 times control and highest-change h9 motion MAE <= 1.05 times control; both anchor proxy retention >= 0.95 and no consecutive missing frames; visual review required
limits: Matched half-sweep exploratory comparison on one training video; replay uses additional labeled examples and extra compute. No posterior, online prediction, cross-video validation, full 168x9 evaluation or teacher acceptance.
